title: Docs program: Model + Agent primitives across ecosystem repos
description: Bring ecosystem documentation up to date and coherent around the new Model primitive (training + evaluation + registry) and the Agent primitive (call pattern, output access, provider/model conventions), across these repos: ../Tactus-web, ../Tactus-examples, ../Learning-Tactus, ../Tactus-in-a-Nutshell, ../Programming-Tactus.\n\nThis epic is structured as: (1) research/scope; (2) holistic concept + vocabulary; (3) outlines/writing notes per repo; (4) implementation edits; (5) CI/links/examples validation.
creator: Ryan Alyn Porter

custom.beads_acceptance_criteria:
- Each repo has an up-to-date, consistent narrative for Model + Agent primitives
- All code snippets match current DSL semantics (result.output, tools=, Model.training, provider/model)
- Example commands are runnable (or explicitly marked as mock/optional ML extras)
- CI green across affected repos
custom.beads_close_reason: Completed ecosystem docs program: updated examples + web + books for Agent/Model primitives; snippets consistent (result.output, tools=, Model.training, model=provider/model); verified builds and CI green across repos
custom.beads_notes:
Docs program plan (Option A, unified + coherent)

North-star: Teach a single coherent mental model across all ecosystem repos:
- Agent primitive = conversational + stateful orchestration (turns, tools, message history).
- Model primitive = stateless prediction interface (input -> output) with a first-class lifecycle: declare -> (optionally) train -> register -> evaluate -> run in procedures.

Canonical conventions (apply everywhere unless a chapter explicitly teaches alternatives):
- Agent calls: agent({...}) returns a result whose primary value is result.output (not result.response/message).
- Prefer LiteLLM-style model strings: model="openai/gpt-4o-mini" and omit provider= unless you are demonstrating the split; provider+model remains supported.
- Tool references live under Agent.tools (not Agent.toolsets).
- Model training config lives under Model.training (single Model block; no separate training file required).
- CI-safe examples must have deterministic specs and run in mock mode (tactus test --mock). Real training is optional and gated behind extras (tactus[ml]/tactus[hf]).

Phases
1) Research + scope (do first):
- For each target repo, locate every page/chapter/example that mentions Agent or Model primitives.
- Record drift types: stale call pattern, stale output accessor, stale CLI flags, stale install guidance, duplicated/competing vocabulary.
- Write repo-specific outlines/writing notes as issues (children of this epic).

2) Holistic narrative + vocabulary (before editing text):
- Define a shared glossary: provider/model, registry-backed model, version/tag, candidate tag, mock mode, CI-safe, training extras.
- Decide a standard example storyline used across repos (IMDB sentiment: Naive Bayes vs HF sequence classifier; same Procedure logic + mocks + deterministic specs).

3) Draft outlines (per repo)
- Tactus-web: landing pages + llms.txt + examples gallery (keep snippets aligned with canonical conventions).
- Tactus-examples: runnable .tac examples + READMEs; align to canonical style; ensure each example states mock vs real requirements.
- Learning-Tactus / Programming-Tactus / Tactus-in-a-Nutshell: chapter-level teaching sequence; add cross-links; keep a single voice + consistent terminology.

4) Implement edits + verify
- Apply changes repo-by-repo; run local build/test gates; watch GitHub Actions with gh.
- Verify all examples still validate; ensure training examples have clear 'optional extras' instructions and graceful error messaging when extras missing.

5) Final coherence pass
- Re-scan all repos for known drift markers (result.response/result.message, toolsets=, provider required, old train/evaluate syntax).
- Ensure all code blocks are runnable as written (or explicitly labeled as pseudocode).
